repo.description: Training library for Megatron-based models with bidirectional Hugging Face conversion capability
repo.name: Megatron-Bridge

detail.body:
## What does this PR do?

Define performance readiness for new base pretraining library recipes and separate diagnostic full recompute from final recipe recommendations. No recompute and cheap selective recompute are equally valid starting choices. Full recompute requires measured capacity need or better end-to-end throughput in matched runs, including any larger MBS or lower TP it enables.

## Changelog

- Apply approximate BF16 targets of 200 model TFLOP/s/GPU on H100 and 400 on GB200 to new pretraining recipes under `src/megatron/bridge/recipes/`. Exclude SFT, PEFT, and long-context SFT. A `perf_recipes` benchmark cannot satisfy this library-recipe requirement. Other precisions/hardware need workload-matched measured targets.
- Withhold severely underperforming library recipes or explicitly mark them early, unoptimized in the recipe, public docs/card, and PR, with measured results and limitations. Include the label in the affected card item's `expected_result` so generated pages display it.
- Update the VLM workflow, examples, GDN caveat, and all four recompute guides. Compare viable layouts at fixed workload, hardware, precision, GBS, and convergence settings; record memory and steady-state performance.
- Identify the VLM card configurations as historical measurements rather than defaults, preserving their values, and align the recipe recommender's fit-then-fill evaluation.

## Validation

- Fresh independent review of the six-file diff: approved, no remaining findings.
- All 72 repository documentation consistency tests passed.
- Full pre-commit checks and `git diff --check` passed.
- Fern 5.40.0 `check`: zero errors; unauthenticated redirects check skipped with a warning.
- Skill validation passed using temporary copies that exclude the VLM skill's unchanged repository-specific `when_to_use` extension; the generic validator rejects that field on both main and this branch.
- VLM YAML and recommender eval JSON parse; historical `best_configs` values are unchanged.

Documentation and evaluation guidance only; no runtime or recipe implementation changes.

inline_comments.body: Should this be scoped to pretrain perf recipes? I checked the card catalog: every H100/GB200 pretrain_performance result clears 200/400, but most SFT/PEFT/long-context ones are under half of it (GB200 SFT 8/8, PEFT 9/9), and cards can't change batch size. As written, an agent would hold back or label pretty much every new SFT/PEFT recipe. Probably also worth saying these are BF16 numbers (the GB200 MXFP8 recipes are at 730-1230, so 400 is a low bar there) and adding something for GB300/B200.

The Qwen3-VL best configs in the VLM card.yaml are all full recompute (~440-470 on GB200/B200), and the llama3 8B H100 perf recipe uses block recompute on 5 layers. Maybe also allow keeping it when a matched run shows it's faster? Same wording is in the other three files.

reviews.body:
Direction makes sense, approving. Two inline comments, neither blocking.

Couple of small follow-ups, fine after merge:
- VLM card.yaml best_configs are all full recompute, which now disagrees with the new "none or cheap selective" line in SKILL.md. The recipe-recommender fit-then-fill eval also still expects "EP8 can still require full recompute" / "prefer selective".
- The early, unoptimized label goes in the card summary, but the generated model pages don't show the summary (it only lands in catalog JSON), so it won't show up there. Putting it in the perf item's expected_result too would fix that.

Also NVSkills CI got skipped here (the auto-request treated it as an untrusted fork PR), so someone needs to trigger it by hand.
